title: Mordheim KB catalogue — catalog/campaign/recruitment-and-veterans.yaml
description: How a warband hires new warriors, when a veteran is available and which rolls the creation of a warband still owes. The policies, the availability roll and the creation tables are rule knowledge; the recruits already hired, the Experience pool and the rolled outcomes of a concrete warband are campaign state and live outside the KB.

recruitment_policy.description: The policies that restrict what a warband may hire or buy at a given moment.

veteran_availability.description: The procedure that says whether an experienced warrior is on the market.

creation_decisions.description: Rolls the printed rules require while a warband is being created. Each one names the band, the rule and the recipient profiles, so an application can demand the roll exactly when the roster holds a recipient and persist only the result.

lifecycle_clauses.description: Roster-lifecycle clauses a printed band rule imposes outside construction. Each one names the trigger the campaign already observes and the profiles it operates on; the operation is a closed vocabulary, so a consumer never reads the rule prose.

succession_clauses.description: Leader-succession clauses a printed band rule imposes. Each one names the leader profile and the eligible successor profiles; the core-book consequence the rule refers to is a separate document.

advance_access_clauses.description: Advancement-time skill-list grants a printed band rule imposes. Each one names the trigger advance, the recipient profiles and the skill lists it adds to their choices.

effect_ids.description: Effects of this catalogue a warband's own special rules may modify.

policy.description: One recruitment policy: prose faithful to the source, plus the structured fields the application needs to apply it.

applies_to.description: The moment the policy governs: hiring a henchman, or the recruit a warband starts with.

scope.description: Machine-readable scope of the policy, when the source states one beyond its prose, e.g. `common_items_only`.

item_id.description: Canonical item the policy is about, when it is about one.

creation_decision.description: One warband-creation roll: who owes it and which printed outcome each dice result reaches. The outcome text is the rule's own wording; an application records the dice result and the outcome id, never a translated sentence.

band_id.description: Band whose creation owes the roll.

rule_id.description: Band rule the roll belongs to.

profile_ids.description: Recipient profiles: the roll is owed while the draft roster holds one of them.

required.description: Whether the warband cannot be committed before the roll is recorded. Defaults to true; declared explicitly so a future optional roll cannot be inferred from prose.

outcomes.description: Printed outcome of each dice interval, in roll order.

creation_outcome.description: One printed result of a creation roll. `result_id` is the stable identity an application persists.

lifecycle_clause.description: One roster-lifecycle clause: when it fires and what it does to the named profiles. `require_member` blocks recruiting other profiles while the named one is missing from the roster; `remove_member` takes the named profile out of the roster when the trigger fires.

rule_id.description: Printed band rule the clause transcribes.

trigger.description: Campaign moment that fires the clause.

profile_ids.description: Profiles the clause operates on, and the only ones it lets through while it is unmet.

succession_clause.description: One leader-succession clause: the profile that leads the band and the profiles the printed rule allows to take over. The core-book consequence the rule refers to is a separate document.

rule_id.description: Printed band rule the clause transcribes.

leader_profile_ids.description: Profiles whose roster member leads the band.

successor_profile_ids.description: Profiles the printed rule allows to take over.

advance_access_clause.description: One advancement-time skill-list grant: the trigger advance, the recipient profiles and the skill lists the printed rule adds to their choices.

rule_id.description: Printed band rule the clause transcribes.

profile_ids.description: Profiles whose choices the grant widens.

skill_lists.description: Skill lists added to the profile's choices.

veteran.description: The veteran availability procedure. The Experience a veteran already carries is not printed here: the KB declares the pool it is drawn from and the price of each point.

roll.description: The roll that decides whether a veteran is available.

experience_pool.description: Where the Experience of the veteran comes from.

allocation.description: How it is allocated, e.g. as advances of the player's choice.

incremental_cost.description: What each Experience point of the veteran costs.

per_experience_point_gc.description: Gold crowns added per Experience point the veteran carries.
